sources.title: John J. Stephan, The Far Eastern Republic: A Product of Intervention
sources.note: Scholarly legal and diplomatic analysis of the buffer republic, Japanese intervention, sovereignty claims and international setting.

sources.title: Government Partners of the Bolsheviks
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of Socialist Revolutionary, Menshevik and Bolshevik cooperation and the limits of constitutional coalition government.

sources.title: 1914-1918 Online, Siberian Intervention, 1918 to 1922
sources.note: Academic encyclopedia synthesis of Allied and Japanese intervention, the buffer strategy, Vladivostok and the 1922 withdrawal.

sources.title: US Department of State, report on Far Eastern Republic organization, May 1920
sources.note: Contemporary diplomatic telegram listing the proclaimed territory, republican form, liberties, parties, nationalities and withdrawal demands.

sources.title: US Department of State, report on Far Eastern Republic unification
sources.note: Contemporary account of Soviet buffer planning, Chita capture, regional representatives, cabinet formation and ongoing fighting.

sources.title: Far Eastern Republic Constituent Assembly declaration, March 1921
sources.note: Primary translated declaration on territory, elections, rights, minorities, land and water, trade, foreign relations and intervention.

sources.title: Harold S. Quigley, Constitution of the Far Eastern Republic
sources.note: Contemporary American Political Science Review analysis of the 1921 constitution, legislature, government and declared civil order.

sources.title: Presidential Library, Basic Law of the Far Eastern Republic, 27 April 1921
sources.note: Official-library catalog and scan of the 72-page Chita edition used to authenticate date, title and original Cyrillic.

sources.title: Electronic Library of Historical Documents, 1921 Far Eastern Republic Constitution
sources.note: Digitized historical document used for the exact Russian Article 1 sample and published constitutional context.

sources.title: Russian archival guides, Far Eastern Republic authorities
sources.note: Official archival authority guide describing the People Assembly, two-year election rules and government structure under the constitution.

sources.title: US Department of State, Japanese demands at Dairen
sources.note: Contemporary record of Japanese demands concerning Vladivostok, commerce, landholding, fortifications, navigation and anticommunism.

sources.title: US Department of State, Japanese memorandum on Siberia
sources.note: Contemporary Japanese diplomatic position on troop withdrawal, security, residents, commerce and negotiations with the Chita government.

sources.title: US Department of State, Far Eastern Republic economic mission
sources.note: Primary diplomatic appeal describing civil rights, private property, free trade, concessions, railways, telegraphs and regional resources.

sources.title: US Department of State, Far Eastern Republic becomes part of Soviet Russia
sources.note: Contemporary telegram recording incorporation, the revolutionary committee and temporary retention of gold currency and compatible laws.

sources.title: Far Eastern Republic People Assembly self-dissolution resolution, 13 November 1922
sources.note: Digitized primary resolution for self-dissolution, restored Soviet authority and reunion with the Russian SFSR.

sources.title: Tatiana Linkhoeva, Revolution Goes East
sources.note: Open scholarly monograph on Japanese intervention, Soviet communism, diplomacy and a Far Eastern Republic telegraph representative in Tokyo.

sources.title: HSE University, Far Eastern Republic as a multi-purpose political project
sources.note: Academic chapter treating the republic as a deliberately flexible political project under civil-war and international constraints.

sources.title: Great Russian Encyclopedia, Far Eastern Republic
sources.note: Scholarly encyclopedia chronology of the 1920 proclamation, buffer government, capital, constitution, territorial changes and 1922 ending.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Civil War and intervention map of the Russian Far East
sources.note: Curated historical map and catalog interpretation of intervention, White forces, missions, rail lines and shifting regional governments.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Eleanor Lord Pray Papers finding aid
sources.note: Archival guide to detailed Vladivostok letters on homes, war, occupation, relief, diverse communities and 1920s Soviet life.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Vladivostok port works album
sources.note: National Library of Russia photographs documenting docks, rail works, ships, barges and construction at the Pacific rail terminus.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Water supply, Vladivostok, 1921
sources.note: Dated American National Red Cross photograph documenting water supply labor in Vladivostok during the republic period.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Dom Smith drawing room in Vladivostok
sources.note: Archival interior drawing from the Pray family collection, used as one bounded example of an affluent urban home.

sources.title: Library of Congress, towns, wharves and rail yards in Manchuria and Vladivostok
sources.note: Photograph collection record for streets, buildings, wharves, locomotives and stored goods in the cross-border urban world.

sources.title: Library of Congress, The Soviet Union, China and Japan: Friends and Enemies
sources.note: Scholarly book chapter documenting multilingual Vladivostok stores, theaters, newspapers, schools, clubs and hospitals in the 1920s.

sources.title: Sechenov University, Healthcare in the Far Eastern Republic
sources.note: Medical-history research on the republic Ministry of Health, civilian and military divisions, councils and Indigenous local institutions.

sources.title: Historical Bulletin, Sanitary and epidemiological service in Primorye, 1920 to 1923
sources.note: Peer-reviewed medical history of cholera, plague, transport routes, quarantine and the Vladivostok sanitary observation station.

sources.title: Primorye Rospotrebnadzor, history of the sanitary service
sources.note: Official institutional chronology with staffing, laboratories, inspectors, disinfectors, sanitary stations and health education dates.

sources.title: US Army Medical Department, sanitation during the Siberian expedition
sources.note: Official historical study of polluted Siberian water, Vladivostok crowding, cholera cases and military public-health measures.

sources.title: Government Measures to Transform Family Life in the Russian Far East
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of marriage, divorce, household policy, gender roles and family transformation during the 1920s and 1930s.

sources.title: Everyday life and leisure in Chita in the 1920s
sources.note: Archive-based urban study of streets, lighting, cleanliness, entertainment and material conditions in the former republic capital.

sources.title: Vladivostok Fortress Museum, history
sources.note: Official museum history records a builders settlement reused as a children shelter with electricity, heat, water and sewerage.

sources.title: Korean and Chinese Settlers and Migrant Workers in the Soviet Far East
sources.note: Peer-reviewed demographic and social study of family migration, labor, Vladivostok communities, citizenship and shifting Soviet policy.

sources.title: Oxford Academic, Transnational World of the Korean Settlement
sources.note: Scholarly borderland history of Korean settlement, citizenship, family life and discriminatory urban policy in the Russian Far East.

sources.title: Cultural, Spatial, and Legal Displacement of the Korean Diaspora in the USSR
sources.note: Peer-reviewed account of the 1937 forced removal of roughly 172,000 Koreans and their restricted lives in Central Asia.

sources.title: Hiroaki Kuromiya, Cleansing the Soviet Far East, 1937 to 1938
sources.note: Scholarly analysis of Korean and Chinese removals, political repression and security policy in the Soviet Far East.

sources.title: Repressive Policy as a Tool of Resolving the Chinese Issue in the USSR
sources.note: Peer-reviewed archival study of anti-Chinese campaigns, status restrictions, NKVD directives and Great Terror repression.

sources.title: YIVO Encyclopedia, Birobidzhan
sources.note: Scholarly reference for the 1928 settlement project, 1934 Jewish autonomous region, Yiddish culture and limited migration.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Go East, Young Jew, Go East
sources.note: Curated map history of the 1928 KOMZET decision, environmental surveys, settlement promotion and 1934 administrative change.

sources.title: Slavic Review, From Savages to Citizens
sources.note: Peer-reviewed analysis of coercive Soviet cultural campaigns among many northern and Far Eastern Indigenous peoples.

sources.title: Inner Asia, Soviet schooling and Evenki children
sources.note: Academic account of Russian-language residential schooling, mobility disruption and state cultural goals affecting Evenki children.

sources.title: Living the dream: Nanai shamanic experiments
sources.note: Peer-reviewed anthropology identifying Nanai Amur homelands, Tungusic language, shamanic practice and early twentieth-century change.

sources.title: Russian Ethnographic Museum, clothing and household life of Amur peoples
sources.note: Museum collection documents early twentieth-century Nivkh and Amur clothing, utensils, food vessels, hunting and ritual objects.

sources.title: UNESCO, Bikin River Valley nomination
sources.note: Cultural landscape documentation of Udege and Nanai forest knowledge, fishing, hunting and longstanding community relationships with land.

sources.title: Echo of Centuries, Tatar school in the Far Eastern Republic
sources.note: Documentary historical study of attempts to organize national Tatar schooling in the republic during 1921 and 1922.

sources.title: Dennis A. Bartels and Alice L. Bartels, When the North Was Red
sources.note: Scholarly book on Soviet Indigenous education, civil-war chronology, boarding schools and far northern cultural transformation.

sources.title: US Department of State, events near Lake Khasan, August 1938
sources.note: Contemporary diplomatic record of the Soviet-Japanese truce dispute at the atlas endpoint near the Korean and Manchurian borders.

sources.title: Russian Academy of Sciences, Forced Migrations in the Soviet Far East
sources.note: Archive-based monograph on deportation, resettlement, special settlements and coercive population policy from the 1920s onward.

sources.title: US Department of State, Far Eastern Republic trade delegation and railway talks
sources.note: Contemporary discussion of Chinese Eastern Railway negotiations, Dairen demands and the Far Eastern Republic trade mission.

sources.title: US Department of State, obligations after Far Eastern Republic amalgamation
sources.note: Contemporary record confirming November 1922 amalgamation with the Russian SFSR and debate over transferred concession obligations.

proposedOverrides.summary: The historical Far Eastern Republic existed from April 1920 to November 1922; the atlas repeats its mainland polygon through 1938 under an inaccurate SSR label.
